html:
Hiaitsiihi is the self-name of the Pirahã, a small Indigenous people on the Maici River in Amazonas, Brazil. They live by fishing, hunting and gathering, and move along the river in small family camps.

Their language is the last living member of the Mura family, and linguists argue over it. The linguist and former missionary Daniel Everett, who lived among them, said it has no words for exact numbers or colours and does not place clauses inside other clauses. Other linguists disagree, and the debate has made the Pirahã well known far beyond Brazil. Their neighbours in the Madeira basin include the Tenharim and Parintintin.
